rationale: C13 plausibly supplied a concrete template for the child. Both are cordial replies to foreign leaders after messages delivered by their foreign ministers; both affirm bilateral friendship and cooperation, address a proposed presidential visit, and defer that visit while expressing hope for a future opportunity. The shared sequence and closely corresponding language are materially more specific than generic diplomatic-letter boilerplate. C09 and C02 share parts of the friendship-and-future-relations framing, but not the child's full diplomatic situation as closely.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I deeply appreciate the warm sentiment for the United States expressed in your personal letter to me which foreign Minister Kosaka handed to Secretary Herter.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Thank you for your cordial [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE], delivered to me by your Foreign Minister, Mr. Fernando Maria Castiella
shared_material.explanation: Both open by acknowledging a cordial personal communication conveyed through the sender's foreign minister.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The partnership existing between Japan and the United States today is built on a solid foundation of common interest, mutual confidence, and mutual trust.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The agreements signed between our two countries in 1953 have produced good results for both of us. I am happy to have this opportunity to express to you my appreciation of the spirit of cooperation with which you have worked with us
shared_material.explanation: Each moves from acknowledging the message to affirming the established bilateral partnership and cooperation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I trust, too, that at some future time I may have an opportunity to accept your cordial invitation.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Your gracious invitation to Mrs. Eisenhower and me to visit your beautiful country ... is greatly appreciated. I hope that some day we shall have the opportunity
shared_material.explanation: This is a close literal and functional correspondence: appreciation of an invitation followed by a noncommittal hope to visit in the future.
